solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Continental fellow in Scotland perhaps, carrying twisted fibre

indicators.note: the fellow is said to be carrying the fibre, so it sits inside his name

parts.note: Euan is a typically Scottish man's name, given as an example
rope is fibre twisted into strands

explanation.surface: A mainland European man living in Scotland, perhaps a craftsman, has some twisted fibre with him.
explanation.definitionFit: Continental in British use means from mainland Europe, so a European.

clue.text: Key question about king's personal attendant

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: the question is placed about, that is around, the king

parts.note: a query is a question
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A vital question concerns the king's personal attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer who attends a member of the British royal family in person.

clue.text: I'm in surrogate ruler's section of army

indicators.note: I'm is placed in the word for a stand-in ruler

parts.note: a regent rules on behalf of an absent or underage monarch
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of belonging to the stand-in ruler's own part of the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a permanent military unit, a division of an army.

clue.text: English reader, a Liberal, relating to voters

parts.note: a lector is a reader, especially one who reads lessons in church or lectures at a university

explanation.surface: An English university reader who is a Liberal takes an interest in voters.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the body of voters, and electoral describes anything concerning it.

clue.text: Obsessive person in teachers' union

definitions.meaning: a ... is a fanatic, as in a fitness ...
the National Union of Teachers in Britain

explanation.surface: A fanatic is active in the teachers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for an enthusiast, and the initials were those of the main British teaching union.

clue.text: Live with copper — 27, possibly

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Instruction to live alongside copper, with a cross-reference to entry 27.
explanation.walkthrough: The 27 is not a cross-reference to another clue; it is the number itself.
explanation.definitionFit: 27 is three multiplied by itself three times, so it is an example of a cube number.

clue.text: Vivid red vehicle belonging to this compiler

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the setter speaking of themselves would say the thing is mine

explanation.surface: The setter shows off their bright red car.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a deep vivid crimson colour, originally a dye from cochineal.

clue.text: Like invigorating air beginning to boost activity at Epsom?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the start of boost is used

parts.note: Epsom Downs is a racecourse, home of the Derby, so racing goes on there

explanation.surface: Fresh air seems to give a lift to the horse-racing at Epsom.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is an English racecourse in Surrey where the Derby is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracing air is cold and fresh in a way that stimulates and refreshes you.

clue.text: Longing to remove initiator of political clean-up

indicators.note: removing a letter means taking it out of the word for a clean-up

parts.note: a purge is a clean-up, especially a political one

indicators.note: the initiator is what starts something, so the first letter of political

explanation.surface: A desire to get rid of whoever started a political purge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove initiator of political' takes P, the first letter of political, out of PURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong desire or yearning for something.

clue.text: Going on for ever about unidentified person outside

indicators.note: the word for everlasting is put about, that is around, the unknown person

parts.note: eternal means lasting for ever
X stands for an unknown person, as in Mr X

explanation.surface: Someone drones on endlessly about a stranger standing outside.
explanation.definitionFit: External means on the outside or exterior of something.

clue.text: Sentimental type initially involved with Marconi

indicators.note: involved here means tangled up, so the letters are mixed
initially means at the start, so only the first letter of type is used

explanation.surface: A soppy character first got mixed up with the radio pioneer Marconi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentimental type' looks like the definition, but only 'Sentimental' is; 'involved' mixes T and MARCONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic describes someone given to idealised, emotional and loving feeling.

clue.text: Confront Helen, a GLC eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or out of line, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to stand up to Helen, an oddball at the Greater London Council.
explanation.walkthrough: The GLC was the Greater London Council, abolished in 1986.
explanation.definitionFit: To challenge someone is to confront them or dispute what they say.

clue.text: Religious female going backwards and forwards

definitions.text: Religious female going backwards and forwards

indicators.note: the word reads the same in both directions, so it is a palindrome

parts.note: a woman in a religious order

explanation.surface: A sister of a religious order paces to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a woman living in a religious order under vows.

clue.text: University man receiving old writing implement still in wrapping

indicators.note: the man's name receives the other letters inside it

parts.note: Ned is a man's name, short for Edward
a pen is used for writing

explanation.surface: A university man gets an old pen as a present, still in its packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unopened has not yet been unwrapped or undone.

clue.text: Rodney relaxed over there

indicators.note: relaxed suggests loosened, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rodney is lounging around somewhere over there.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old word meaning at a distance, in that place.

clue.text: A Roman senator originally abandoned one on the river

indicators.note: abandoned means unrestrained or wild, so the letters are mixed up
originally means at the start, so only the first letter of senator is used

explanation.surface: A Roman senator was first left behind by someone rowing on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' mixes the letters of A ROMAN with S from 'senator originally'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oarsman is a rower, someone found on the river with an oar.

clue.text: Just rewards — puddings. by the sound of it

indicators.note: this tells us the answer is pronounced like the word for puddings

parts.note: desserts are puddings, the sweet course

explanation.surface: Getting puddings is the fair reward someone has earned.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is 'just deserts', from deserve, not the dry places nor the sweet course.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserts here means what one deserves, as in getting one's just deserts.

clue.text: Get even with archdeacon in maturity

indicators.note: the archdeacon's title goes in the word for maturity

parts.note: age can mean maturity, the state of being grown up
Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Someone finally settles a score with an archdeacon in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to take revenge and so get even with the wrongdoer.

clue.text: Take advantage of former plan to tour India

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the plan goes round, as if touring, the letter for India

parts.note: a plot is a plan or scheme
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Make the most of an old scheme for a trip around India.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it, often unfairly, for your own benefit.

clue.text: Greek character returned and dined

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letter's name is read backwards

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man came back and had dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Ate is the past tense of eat, so it matches dined in tense and meaning.

clue.text: Sound money getting father something to suck

indicators.note: sound here means said aloud, so the slang word for money is used only for how it is pronounced

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
pop is an informal name for father

explanation.surface: Solid cash buys Dad a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it signals a word said aloud: LOLLY, British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard sweet on a stick that you suck.

clue.text: A chap crossing Morecambe, maybe, one from the States

indicators.note: the chap stretches across the other name, holding it inside

parts.note: a man is a chap
Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, so Eric is an example of a Morecambe

explanation.surface: A man travelling across the seaside town of Morecambe turns out to be from the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a Lancashire resort, but here it is the surname of comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: An American is a citizen or native of the United States.

clue.text: Imitate a dove? Goodness me

definitions.meaning: to make the soft call of a dove

explanation.surface: Someone asked to make dove noises reacts with surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Coo names a dove's murmuring call and is also an old-fashioned British cry of astonishment.

clue.text: Knowledgeable about Shintoism? Not entirely

indicators.note: only part of the religion's name is taken, the letters lying within it

explanation.surface: Does someone know a lot about the Japanese religion of Shinto? Only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: To be into a subject is informally to be keen on and well versed in it.

clue.text: Responsibility of bachelor abandoning extra benefit

indicators.note: the extra payment abandons, or leaves out, the bachelor's letter

parts.note: a bonus is an extra benefit or payment

explanation.surface: A single man gives up his bonus and takes on the burden instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Onus is a burden or duty, the obligation that rests on someone.

clue.text: Change too much? About time to retire!

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for time is turned round

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Christmastide

explanation.surface: Should a weary editor change things too much? It is about time they retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' reverses TIDE to give EDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To overedit text is to revise or alter it more than it needs.
